proposals.relationship: Todorov credits Barthes’s receptive teaching and intellectual exchanges with amplifying students’ ideas during his early French literary formation.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1997P11 describes admiration, theoretical humility and active improvement of students’ ideas, not merely thesis supervision. P15 says Barthes’s works played an important role while distinguishing Todorov’s later truth-regulated dialogue from what he thinks Barthes would share. Genette/Bremond/Metz network retains shared credit. Spanish interview rendering/translator unestablished; no complete Barthes originals read.

proposals.relationship: Todorov recalls Lévi-Strauss’s clear rational argument and movement between detailed analysis and bold generalization as an admired model in his structuralist formation.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2001 reply in2003translated samplefooter8 praises precisely these qualities while saying personal contact was rare and kinship/myth studies differed from his literary interests. It also qualifies later scientific ambitions and relativism. Admired intellectual model, not direct mentorship, wholesale allegiance or claim all remembered reading was contemporaneous. La Pensée sauvage1962/Anthropologie structurale1958 identified bynotes13–14, original bodies unread.

proposals.relationship: Todorov questions Lévi-Strauss’s sweeping scientific ambitions and some claims about cultural relativism and the subject, while retaining admiration for his analytical reasoning.
proposals.evidence_note: Own translated retrospectivefooter8 explicitly recalls a critical study later included in Nous et les autres and states that peremptory claims seemed to exceed Lévi-Strauss’s own best thought. Not a report that Lévi-Strauss replied: Todorov says there was no reaction. Exact underlying chapter and full original anthropological works unread. Source is2001interview/2003Spanishedition, not a falsely contemporaneous1960s objection.

proposals.relationship: Todorov identifies Weber’s ideal types and analyses as attractive resources within his renewed study of political philosophy for Nous et les autres.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1997P21 distinguishes useful reading from agreement with every author. It names Strauss’s natural-right dispute and Aron’s introduction as surrounding interpretive mediation, then explicitly states attraction to Weber’s ideal types/analyses. Max Weber, not Eugen Weber. Cited original works unread; no assertion all political-philosophical reading had one source or first-reading date.

proposals.relationship: Todorov resists Weber’s agonistic account of war and the ultimate incompatibility of values, preferring dialogue and a horizon of universality.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1997P21 directly qualifies his appreciation of ideal types and describes the disputed stance as Weber’s Nietzscheanism. This is Todorov’s interpretation, not independent verification that it exhausts Weber. Strauss/Aron debate contextual mediation retained; originals unread and no invented direct exchange.

proposals.relationship: Todorov questions the coherence between Derrida’s democratic commitments and deconstruction’s treatment of values, while acknowledging the theory’s internal sophistication.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1997P25 explicitly locates his objection between public ethical commitments and professional philosophy, not an internal logical refutation. Blanchot’s anti-value statement supplies a separate example, not a quote assigned to Derrida. P27 retains friendship/intellectual admiration but says Derrida did not answer his philosophical interests. Spanish rendering; underlying Derrida/Blanchot texts unread.

proposals.relationship: Todorov adapts Arendt’s banality-of-evil argument when explaining his own emphasis on ordinary acts of good rather than exceptional heroism.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1997P37 explicitly calls his banality of good similar and contrary to Arendt’s argument yet grounded in the same reasons; conceptual adaptation, not simple disagreement or denial of evil. P21 separately names Arendt among a plural philosophical education without implying full agreement. Eichmann book and fullFacingExtreme originals unread; interviewer’s framing distinguished.

proposals.relationship: Todorov challenges Horkheimer and Adorno’s pessimistic Enlightenment narrative for treating a real but avoidable historical development as if it had to culminate in totalitarianism.
proposals.evidence_note: Actual own answer in opening2016 interview, published2020, names both coauthors; Horkheimer lacks endpoint but shared responsibility retained. Todorov concedes shadows and potential threats of Enlightenment, so this is not denial of its destructive uses. Only displayed opening read; original Dialectic and rest of interview unread. Precise question supplied instead of fabricated page.

proposals.relationship: Leichter reports Ricœur’s approving use of Todorov’s warning that claims to victim status can generate demands on others, within Ricœur’s distinction between justice for other victims and self-victimization.
proposals.evidence_note: Explicitly named2012scholarly mediation124–125/nn68–69 directs to English Memory, History, Forgetting86. Neither Ricœur’s original French2000 nor Blamey/Pellauer2004English body nor original Todorovwarning freshly read. This scoped quotation/use is not broad agreement on every duty-of-memory issue, and does not make Leichter an original formative source.

proposals.relationship: Todorov describes introducing Russian Formalist approaches into French literary debate through his1965 translated anthology and subsequent editorial work with Jakobson.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1997P13–15 details translation/selection, Genette’s editorial introduction, Sollers/Pleynet’s publication role and Jakobson’s advice/preface;2001 interviewsample6–7 describes continued editing/translation assistance. Scoped contribution to linguistic literary inquiry, not membership in every poststructuralist position. Later dialogical/ethical departure and criticism of deconstruction retained; no generic biography-based route.

proposals.relationship: Todorov criticises Lacan’s opaque and seductive style as contrary to his own ethical commitment to clarity, rational argument and readers’ capacity to answer.
proposals.evidence_note: Own translated retrospective sample8–9 explicitly states this intellectual and communicative objection. The personal encounter is his recollection, not independent proof of Lacan’s psychology; the claim is limited to Todorov’s criticism of style and intellectual authority. He distinguishes his sustained interest in Freud and admiration for Lévi-Strauss from his response to Lacan. Full Lacan texts unread.

proposals.relationship: Todorov credits reading Habermas, among several interlocutors, with his renewed education in political philosophy for Nous et les autres.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1997P21 explicitly describes these authors as a second university and identifies Habermas/Aron with a Kantian universalist orientation. This is a plural, qualified reading resource rather than allegiance to every position or a claim of personal contact. Arendt, Strauss, Berlin, Aron and Bénichou retain their distinct roles; no full Habermas original freshly read.
